content: Rimantadine is a medication prescribed to prevent and treat infections caused by the influenza A virus. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses. If you have questions about its use, consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Rimantadine is available in tablet and liquid forms, which are taken orally. It is typically taken once or twice daily for a duration of 2 to 12 weeks. A flu vaccine will also be administered alongside this medication. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions or need clarification. Take rimantadine exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Before starting rimantadine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to rimantadine or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially acetaminophen, aspirin, cimetidine (Tagamet), and any vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had liver disease, seizures, or blood disorders. Additionally, inform your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking rimantadine, contact your doctor immediately. Rimantadine may cause stomach upset. To minimize this, take the medication with food or milk. If you forget to take a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Rimantadine may cause side effects. Mild side effects include upset stomach, nervousness, tiredness, difficulty sleeping or concentrating, and lightheadedness. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Severe side effects include skin rash, yellowing of the skin or eyes, mood changes, mental confusion, and vision changes. If you experience any of these severe symptoms, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store rimantadine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor will order specific lab tests to monitor your response to rimantadine. Do not share your medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If you still have symptoms of infection after completing the course of rimantadine, contact your doctor.
